report: Painless left visual blurring, left IOP 42 mmHg with open angles, cup-to-disc 0.9, left RAPD, and severe asymmetric field loss indicate glaucomatous optic neuropathy. Negative neuroimaging and absent proptosis/bruit exclude secondary mass or vascular causes. Cataract coexists but cannot explain the full picture. Radiologist's recommendation to lower IOP supports left primary open-angle glaucoma. Confidence is high but below certainty pending OCT, dynamic IOP, and pachymetry.
